# 1500 W Wilson Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN: 14171060250000 | Uptown (Community Area 3)**

---

## 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B1-2** — a Neighborhood Shopping District with a dash-2 bulk/density designation. The classification comes from the City's official GIS parcel layer and can be verified on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

## 2. Residential Uses: Above-Grade and Ground-Floor Apartments

**Above ground floor:** Dwelling units located above the ground floor are **permitted by-right (P)** in B1 districts [3]. So yes — apartments above ground-floor retail are allowed without any special approval.

**Ground floor:** Dwelling units located *below the second floor* (i.e., on the ground floor) follow a more restricted path [3]. In B1 districts, ground-floor residential is generally **not permitted by-right** in the same fashion. Additionally, [4] notes that in B and C districts within 2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station, newly established detached houses and two-flats are prohibited (though multi-unit residential is preferred where density standards allow). The conversion of an occupied or vacant commercial space below the second floor into residential units is a specific exception that may be approved by the Zoning Administrator under certain conditions [2].

> **Bottom line:** Upper-floor apartments above retail — yes, by right. Ground-floor residential — not straightforwardly permitted by-right in B1; consult the Zoning Administrator or a zoning attorney for the specific pathway.

---

## 3. Bulk and Density Standards

The context does not include the full zone_definition table for B1-2 (it was not returned), so I **cannot state precise FAR, maximum height, minimum lot area per dwelling unit, or setback figures** from the retrieved data. What I can confirm from the code text:

- The B1 district uses "dash" bulk/density designations — the **"-2"** in B1-2 sets the specific FAR, height, and lot-area-per-unit standards per the table at [2] (§ 17-3-0403-A), but that table's numeric rows were not included in the retrieved chunks.
- FAR for transit-served locations with a **FAR increase** is available only in **B-3 and C-3 districts** (i.e., dash-3 designated districts), not in B1-2. See item 6 below.
- To verify exact B1-2 standards, consult the City of Chicago Zoning Ordinance Table at [§ 17-3-0403](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago_zoning_ordinance.html) or call the Dept. of Planning & Development (DPD) at 312-744-5777.

---

## 4. Overlays and Special Designations

All overlays below are confirmed from the City's GIS regulatory layers:

- **Transit-Oriented Development — CTA and Metra:** This parcel is within a TOD overlay for *both* CTA and Metra rail. The nearest CTA station is **Montrose (Brown Line)**, ~0.45 miles away; the nearest Metra station is **Ravenswood (Union Pacific North)**, ~0.39 miles away. The parcel is confirmed `in_tod_area = true`. Transit-served location criteria under [4] (§ 17-3-0308) apply to any new construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or Metra rail station entrance.

- **ADU Eligible Area:** This parcel falls within the City's ADU (Accessory Dwelling Unit) eligible area — meaning accessory dwelling units (coach houses, basement units, etc.) may be permissible subject to ADU ordinance requirements.

- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** The parcel is in an ARO zone. Residential projects triggering an "entitlement" (e.g., a zoning map amendment or planned development) must comply with the ARO's affordable unit or fee requirements [2]. Uptown already has 20 ARO-related affordable housing projects totaling 976 units in the community area, including large projects like the Ruth Shriman House (231 units), Leland Apts. (137 units), and Harold Washington Apts. (100 units).

- **Special Service Area — Greater Ravenswood (SSA):** The parcel is within the Greater Ravenswood Special Service Area, which levies a supplemental property tax for neighborhood commercial services. This is reflected in the tax breakdown — City of Chicago Special Service Area 31 adds an estimated **$395/year** to the property tax bill.

- **No Planned Development, Landmark, Historic, or Lakefront Protection:** The parcel is not in a planned development, not a landmark building, not in a landmark or historic district, not on the National Register, and not subject to Lakefront Protection Ordinance restrictions.

- **Not on a Pedestrian Street:** The parcel is *not* designated on a pedestrian street, which relaxes some of the pedestrian-street storefront requirements under [4] (§ 17-3-0504).

---

## 5. Parking Requirement and Transit Reduction

Because this parcel is in a confirmed CTA transit-served location, the **minimum parking requirement can be reduced by up to 100%** under [2] (§ 17-10-0102-B). In practical terms, for a transit-served B1-2 parcel, you may be able to provide **zero off-street parking** for a qualifying project — this applies by right and does **not** require a Type 1 map amendment or planned development entitlement.

> The 100% parking reduction is the most significant transit benefit available at this specific zoning classification.

---

## 6. Maximum Height, FAR, and What Transit Proximity Enables

**What transit does NOT change at B1-2:**

The **FAR increase for transit-served locations** under [2] (§ 17-3-0403-B) applies **only in B-3 and C-3 districts** (meaning dash-3 designated parcels — e.g., B1-3, B2-3, B3-3 — *not* B1-2). This parcel's dash-2 designation means:
- **No FAR bonus** from transit proximity — by right.
- **No height bonus** from transit proximity — by right.
- **No density bonus** — `density_bonus_eligible` is confirmed false for this parcel.

To access a transit-related FAR increase, the parcel would need to be rezoned to a dash-3 district, which requires a **Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment**, a **Planned Development** approval, or an ARO entitlement as defined in [2] (§ 2-44-085). None of these are available by right.

**What I could not determine:** The precise maximum FAR, height limit, and minimum lot area per dwelling unit for B1-2 were not included in the retrieved code chunks. The dash-2 standard table (§ 17-3-0401 / § 17-3-0403-A) would contain these numbers. Given this parcel's land area of approximately 4,347 sq ft and building footprint of 43,790 sq ft (note: the building square footage is sourced from commercial valuation, which may reflect the full multi-story building — the footprint is 1 story per county records), the FAR relationship between land and permitted building area is the key figure to confirm with DPD.
